public_rationale: The search found venture financing and reports about startup margins, but neither establishes the claimed dependency for the specified customers. A startup may raise money while covering model bills from sales, or temporarily fund deficits from existing cash. Without cohort membership and cash-flow records, the causal claim cannot be settled.
limitations: Private customer finances are incompletely disclosed.
Gross profit, operating cash flow, and venture financing measure different things.
The unspecified accounting basis also prevents a decisive financial comparison.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that the relevant startup customers cannot sustain their model payments without additional venture financing.
Receiving venture funding does not by itself establish that customer receipts cannot cover model bills.
The surrounding discussion narrows attention to startups subsidizing customers' token consumption, but it does not identify which members of Ramp's top 1% qualify.
Use August 2026, the last complete month before publication, as the reference period for the asserted ongoing dependency.
No accounting basis is supplied for the asserted dependency.
criteria.support_condition: Identified startups in the relevant spending cohort have recurring cash deficits that make continued payments to the labs dependent on further venture funding, after accounting for existing cash and other financing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Financial records show the relevant startups can sustain their model payments from customer cash receipts or other durable resources without additional venture funding.
